evidence: The hunk deletes `_capabilities` and `capabilities()` from RouterEngine while the class docstring still said '[`voices`] and [`capabilities`] are reads'; 1468171 rewrites it to say only `voices` is a read and points at Voice.capabilities.
guidance_note: When deleting a method, grep the repo for every bracketed reference to its name (docstrings, README, package docstring) and update them in the same commit.

evidence: DeclaredEngine stamped one set over all voices, so no single-engine divergence test existed; writing one exposed a real bug (speak_timed and _length still read self._capabilities). The agent chose an inherit-if-empty rule rather than the reviewer's per-voice mapping, and that rule is what F11 then caught as conflating empty with unset.
guidance_note: When a field moves from the engine to each voice, migrate the test double's internals (every read of the old engine-wide field) in the same commit and add a fixture whose voices differ.

evidence: `declared()` is a union, so `TIMESTAMPS in declared(engine)` proves only one voice carries it; 1468171 replaces it with `all(... for v in engine.voices())`.
guidance_note: When asserting a property that is claimed for every element, assert it per element rather than against an aggregate like a union.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 on the same RouterEngine docstring naming the deleted `capabilities` method; fixed by the same 1468171 edit.
Third duplicate of F1 on the same docstring; same fix in 1468171.

`headers()` now passes `honoured(resolution.voice)` while `_NEEDS_CAPABILITY`'s comment and `_honoured`'s docstring still said 'the engine's declaration' and 'The capability half genuinely is fixed'; 1468171 rewrites both to the speaking voice.
guidance_note: When changing where a fact is read from (engine to voice), search for the old phrasing ('engine's declaration', 'fixed at startup') across docstrings and README before pushing.

evidence: The hunk shows `_model_json(model_id, offered()) for model_id in directory.listed()`, recomputing the union per entry; 1468171 hoists it to `deployment_wide = offered()`.
guidance_note: When replacing a precomputed value with a function call, check whether the call site sits inside a loop.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: 1468171 touched api.py, router.py, conftest and tests only, while the open()-only stamping in piper.py/kokoro.py came from the original PR. acquire() returned `ready.voice` unstamped, so the same voice id carried different capabilities from acquire and open; 012f7fc derives both from one helper.
guidance_note: When making a field part of a type's truthful description, find every constructor/lifecycle path that produces that type (acquire and open) and stamp it in all of them.

evidence: F3's fix added a per-voice assertion for kokoro only; piper's open() stamps over the same kind of loop and every capability test in test_piper.py opened one voice. 012f7fc adds the multi-voice piper test.
guidance_note: When a reviewer names a coverage gap for one engine, apply the same assertion to every engine that shares the code shape before replying Fixed.

evidence: The mandatory-capabilities check in remote._voice is original-PR code (1468171 did not touch remote.py), so the flag is anchoring only. The stale-backend stub omitted capabilities, so it tripped the new voice check before reaching engine_name(); 012f7fc adds capabilities to the stub and pins the 'what engine it runs' message.
guidance_note: When adding a new validation that runs earlier than an existing one, rerun the tests for the later check and pin each to its specific message so one cannot silently satisfy another.

evidence: 1468171 (the F2 fix) added `voice if voice.capabilities else replace(...)`, so an explicitly empty voice was silently promoted to the engine default. The agent removed the sentinel entirely instead of the reviewer's None sentinel: DeclaredEngine now takes finished voices plus a `declaring()` helper.
guidance_note: Before using a value's emptiness as 'not stated', check whether empty is a legal stated value of that field; if it is, the type needs another shape.

evidence: 1468171 switched speak_timed and _length from `self._capabilities` to `voice.capabilities` but kept the `self._capabilities = capabilities` assignment, leaving it unread; 012f7fc deletes it.
guidance_note: After moving every reader of an attribute elsewhere, delete the attribute in the same commit.

evidence: The F3 fix in 1468171 added a comment about 'one of the four' and 'three voices' while the fixture loads KOKORO_VOICES with two; 012f7fc drops the count.
guidance_note: When a fix's comment states a count, check it against the fixture it describes, or leave the count out.

evidence: 012f7fc (the F11 fix) added 'It takes finished voices rather than a capability set' but left the [LAW:one-type-per-behavior] paragraph saying 'One type taking a capability set'; f4fb90e rewrites it.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a constructor signature, reread the whole class docstring, not just the paragraph being added.

evidence: 012f7fc did not touch __init__.py, so the flag itself is anchoring. The package docstring's 'voices, capabilities, and the two synthesis calls' is the same stale reference to the removed method that F1 fixed only in router.py; f4fb90e fixes it.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags one stale reference to a removed API, grep for every remaining reference before fixing just the flagged one.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the README hunk is original-PR text, and 012f7fc did not touch README. The new per-voice `capabilities` field on GET /v1/voices was undocumented for callers; f4fb90e adds a section.
guidance_note: When a PR adds a field to a public HTTP response, document it in the caller-facing endpoint docs, not only in the implementer section.

evidence: The F10 fix in 012f7fc added `capabilities` to the stale stub so it reaches /v1/models, which removed the only test that hit the 'no capabilities' branch; the agent concedes it 'moved coverage rather than adding it'. f4fb90e adds a dedicated test.
guidance_note: When editing a fixture so a test stops hitting branch A, add a test for branch A in the same commit.

evidence: The README /v1/models row saying 'what it will honour' was untouched by 012f7fc, so the flag is anchoring. It is the same deployment-wide-capability phrasing F6 fixed only in api.py docstrings; under per-voice capabilities it is now only a union. f4fb90e rewrites the row.
guidance_note: When a semantic shift (per-engine to per-voice) is flagged in one docstring, sweep README and every user-facing description of the same fact.

evidence: README rule 2 said the ignored list is 'worked out per request from the engine behind the server', the same per-engine framing F6 corrected only in api.py; f4fb90e rewrites it to 'the voice that will speak'.
guidance_note: When fixing stale per-engine wording in code, grep README for the same phrasing ('the engine') in the same commit.

evidence: f4fb90e did not touch test_conformance.py, so the flag is anchoring. The F2 fix added divergence coverage only in test_capabilities.py, while every ENGINES subject stamped one set and the tests used first_voice. 1abdf5f adds a voices-differ subject and iterates one voice per distinct claim instead of every voice, with a cost reason.
guidance_note: When a bug is found in a test double's per-element wiring, add the diverging subject to the shared conformance suite, not only to a one-off test.

evidence: f4fb90e touched no api.py, so the flag is anchoring. The inline comment on `capabilities` still said 'this deployment will actually honour'; that is the same union-vs-per-voice claim F18 fixed in the README row but not here. 1abdf5f shortens it to the union framing.
guidance_note: When fixing a 'what it will honour' claim in one place, grep for the same phrase in code comments beside the field it describes.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 1abdf5f changed only api.py and test_conformance.py, and the _fleet docstring widening was original-PR text. voices() and engine_name() are two sequential HTTP requests, so 'cannot come from two different moments' was false; 353ca69 rewrites the docstring to state the gap and why it is tolerable.
guidance_note: When splitting one request into two, re-examine every atomicity claim in the surrounding docstrings.

narrative: A cross-cutting move of capabilities from Engine to Voice ran into the 5-round cap. Every finding was valid and accepted. Most later-round findings were either fix-introduced defects (the inherit-if-empty sentinel in the F2 fix, a dead attribute, a wrong count comment, a fixture edit that dropped coverage) or the same stale per-engine wording left in places the first fix did not sweep. Several ON-NAMED-FIX flags were anchoring artifacts on original-PR text (F8, F10, F16, F22). Round 5 was a cap notice, not a review.
guidance_observations: The original PR removed Engine.capabilities() without grepping for remaining references, and the stale mentions surfaced one at a time across rounds 0, 2 and 3.
Fixes were scoped to the exact line flagged; the sibling engine (piper vs kokoro) and sibling docs (README, __init__, inline comments) were each left for the next round.
The agent verified fixes by mutation (reverting the stamp, stamping only the first voice), which made the round-1 tests trustworthy even when the surrounding design still needed iteration.

evidence: `_aliases_of` returns `carried | load_aliases(name, voices)` with a documented file-wins precedence, and the reviewer reports no test of the collision. The PR was closed unmerged because the alias mechanism's premise died, so no response is defensible; had it continued, a test was owed.
guidance_note: When a docstring states a precedence rule, add the test that would fail if the precedence flipped.

evidence: `str(alias) for alias in published.get("aliases") or ()` has no isinstance check: a string is iterated char by char and an int raises a bare TypeError, unlike the list check on `capabilities` above it. The PR was closed deliberately before any response.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a wire parser that shape-checks its other fields, copy the same isinstance-and-ConfigError guard for the new field.

evidence: Duplicate of F2 on the same line: `aliases` lacks the list check that `capabilities` has. PR closed unmerged for an unrelated reason.

The tie-break test only asserts `[voice.id for voice in engine.voices()][0] == "af_heart"`, which is discovery order, and never resolves `rachel` through a Catalog or the app, so a last-wins regression in `_aliases_of` would pass. PR closed unmerged.
guidance_note: Test a tie-break by resolving the contested key through the code that implements it, not by checking the input ordering it consumes.

evidence: Third duplicate of F2: unchecked `aliases` shape contradicts the function's 'the wire's shape is checked here, once' claim. PR closed unmerged.
Duplicate of F4: the test asserts voices() order rather than which voice `rachel` resolves to. PR closed unmerged.
`if str(alias)` filters after conversion, so a JSON null becomes the truthy alias 'None' and numbers become strings; the hunk shows exactly that expression. PR closed unmerged.
guidance_note: When filtering wire items, test the raw value's type before converting it, never the converted value's truthiness.

evidence: Duplicate of F7: `str(None) == "None"` passes the `if str(alias)` filter. PR closed unmerged.

The test comment ties `x-elvenspeak-voice-requested` to 'a substitution happened', and with FIRST_OFFERED and one voice a fallback is also a substitution, which supports the reviewer. The packet does not show Catalog.resolve to confirm it sets substituted identically on both branches. PR closed unmerged.
guidance_note: When a test claims to distinguish path A from path B, construct the fixture so path B would produce a different observable result (e.g. Substitution.OFF or a second voice).

narrative: One review round with nine findings (four distinct issues plus duplicates), none answered. The PR was closed as a deliberate non-merge because the alias mechanism it extended lost its rationale (ElevenLabs ids will not be used), citing carrying-cost. The findings were real: unchecked `aliases` wire shape, str-then-filter admitting 'None', and tie-break and precedence tests that did not exercise the merge code.
guidance_observations: The wire-parsing gaps would have been avoided by copying the existing `capabilities` isinstance guard when adding the sibling field.
Closing with an issue comment rather than leaving the threads open was the right handling of a dead premise.

evidence: No test drove MuteEngine through /stream/with-timestamps; the agent measured a `RuntimeError: ... response already started` and eb45c8f adds a test pinning that abort.
guidance_note: When a docstring admits one path behaves differently from the rest, add a test pinning that path's actual behavior in the same PR.

evidence: The reviewer was unsure; the agent ran it and got 'response already started' even for the first sentence, so 'after its first object' overstated the protection. eb45c8f rewrites the _silent_engine docstring.
guidance_note: Measure framework behavior (here, when StreamingResponse commits its status) before writing a docstring that claims a window of protection.

evidence: speak_timed and _synthesized each had their own `except ValueError ... _EMPTY_REDUCTION` block; eb45c8f extracts `_created` and both callers use it.
guidance_note: When adding the same exception translation to a second entry point, extract the shared helper rather than copying the try/except.

evidence: _Crashing implemented only `create`, so speak_timed's catch was untested; eb45c8f adds `create_timed` and two end-to-end speak_timed tests.
guidance_note: When a fix touches two entry points, write the test pair for each entry point, not only the first one.

evidence: `EVERYTHING = frozenset({Capability.SPEED, Capability.TIMESTAMPS})` hand-lists the enum while conftest uses `frozenset(Capability)`; eb45c8f derives it.
guidance_note: When a constant's name means 'all members', derive it from the enum.

evidence: `_language(voice.id)` runs while building the create() arguments, before the stub raises, and 'fake-voice' survived only because 'f' maps to French; eb45c8f uses a local `KOKORO_VOICE` with id af_test.
guidance_note: When a unit test calls into an engine, give it an input built to that engine's own grammar rather than a cross-module generic fixture.

evidence: `from elvenspeak.voices import Substitution` was unused in test_silence.py; eb45c8f removes it.
guidance_note: Run the linter's unused-import check before pushing a new test file copied from another.

evidence: 'zero-size array to reduction operation' is numpy's shared prefix for every identity-less reduction; eb45c8f narrows it to '... maximum' and adds a 'minimum' test, which the agent verified goes red under the old constant.
guidance_note: When matching an exception by message, include the part of the message that identifies the specific call site, and test that a sibling message is not caught.

evidence: eb45c8f corrected _silent_engine's four-endpoint overclaim for F2 but left `Silence`'s docstring saying 'the four synthesis endpoints all have to turn it into the same answer'; db2ec3f drops the count.
guidance_note: When correcting an overclaimed guarantee in one docstring, grep for the same claim ('four ... endpoints') in every related docstring before pushing.

narrative: The PR adds a Silence checkpoint and kokoro empty-output translation. Round 0 raised eight valid findings, all fixed in one commit with mutation-verified tests. The only fix-linked finding was F9: the F2 docstring correction did not sweep the identical four-endpoint claim on the Silence class. Fixing that triggered round 2, which approved.
guidance_observations: The agent measured the Starlette behavior instead of reasoning about it, which settled a low-confidence finding decisively.
Round 0's duplicated catch (F3) and missing timed-path tests (F4) were both avoidable by extracting the helper at the moment the second entry point was added.

evidence: `_heard` treated any 502 as silence, while a proxy between router and backend can emit an unrelated 502. The reviewer offered confirm-or-document; the agent instead stamped a `Silence.WIRE_HEADER` on elvenspeak's own 502 and classifies on that header. It added a test with an unstamped 502 that reds when the status-only check is restored.
guidance_note: When decoding a generic status code as a domain signal, ask who else on the path can emit that code and carry an explicit marker if anyone can.

narrative: One finding on mapping a bare 502 to Silence. The agent rejected the document-the-topology option and made the signal a fact about the responder via a stamped header, which removed the status-number condition entirely. Round 1 approved with no findings.
guidance_observations: The agent's original comment asserted '502 is written in exactly one place' about its own code while the decision depended on the whole network path, a premise it could have checked before the first push.

evidence: `job in required` was a substring test on the raw `[reachability, tests]` text, so `integration-tests` would satisfy `tests`. The fix parses into a frozenset of names and adds a test that constructs that case. It was proven load-bearing and also verified on the forge.
guidance_note: When a test reads a list out of config text, parse it into discrete names before checking membership.

evidence: The generalized docstring said 'the file is what the forge executes' for both files, but MERGE_GATE runs on GitHub, not the Gitea forge. The packet shows this in the PR-wide hunk with no flag and no reviewed-against commit, so it reads as original-PR text. bd5824e rewords it per runner.
guidance_note: When generalizing a sentence from one subject to several, check that each clause is still true of every subject.

narrative: The PR adds a tests job to the Gitea publish gate. Round 0 found a substring membership check that could pass over a dropped gate; the agent parsed it properly and verified on the forge. Round 1 found an original-PR docstring that called GitHub 'the forge', fixed in bd5824e, and round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: Neither finding was caused by a fix; both were original-PR defects the reviewer surfaced in successive rounds.
